item.title: Research progress of gene correction for genetic diseases via in vivo prime editing.
item.abstract: Curative therapies for genetic diseases caused by pathogenic mutations demand precise and safe genome editing technologies. Prime editing (PE), a CRISPR-Cas9-derived technology that enables precise base conversions without double-strand breaks (DSBs), has emerged as a transformative tool with the ability to correct 89% of human pathogenic mutations. However, transitioning PE from preclinical models to clinical applications faces critical challenges, particularly in the development of in vivo delivery systems and scalable manufacturing. This review systematically summarizes advances of in vivo PE therapeutics, focusing on the therapeutic outcomes across some retinal, metabolic, and hematologic genetic diseases. We further dissect barriers to clinical translation, including in the immunogenicity of viral vectors, off-target risks in nondividing cells, and large-scale production bottlenecks. By highlighting the unique advantages of in vivo PE and proposing actionable solutions for scalable manufacturing, the work provides a roadmap for accelerating in vivo PE-based therapies toward clinical reality.

item.title: Precision meets scale: DSB- and recombinase-free targeted insertion of large DNA fragments.
item.abstract: Targeted insertion of large DNA fragments has been constrained by the genotoxicity associated with double-strand breaks (DSBs) and the limitations of two-step recombinase systems. Three independently developed mammalian platforms, Quadruple pegRNA (QuadPE), Prime Assembly (PA), and PRIME-In, now achieve programmable, DSB- and recombinase-free insertion of up to 26 kb, 11.3 kb, and 9.2 kb, respectively, through convergent yet mechanistically distinct flap-guided integration strategies. Notably, QuadPE and PA achieve integration independent of cell-cycle progression. Furthermore, these systems outperform several existing recombinase- and/or transposase-based tools, underscoring their translational potential for therapeutic utility. Their mechanistic logic also provides a forward path for the DSB-free and recombinase-free integration of large DNA sequences in crop biotechnology.

item.title: Simulating Directed Evolution In Silico with an Iterative, Physics-Based Workflow.
item.abstract: Directed evolution consistently delivers engineered enzymes that facilitate diverse biocatalytic transformations. Despite advances in automation and high-throughput workflows, our ability to rapidly engineer novel enzymes is limited by our inability to thoroughly sample the vast protein design space. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) methods have alleviated this challenge to some degree, due to their ability to propose mutations based on learned patterns from complex protein data sets. However, the hidden logic of these AI-based methods can complicate our ability to reveal and exploit fundamental details of these enzymes. To complement these hidden-logic models, we present a structure- and physics-based workflow that mimics directed evolution in silico. This Virtual Protein EngineeR (referred to as ViPER) aims to simulate directed evolution by leveraging computational modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, in silico mutagenesis, and structure-based property evaluation to iteratively engineer an enzyme toward a desired target. In this work, we present a retrospective analysis to demonstrate ViPER's ability to efficiently navigate the complex protein-protein interfaces associated with the oligomerization of a ketoreductase (KRED) enzyme. In addition to successfully predicting >70% of sites that are crucial for toggling the oligomerization of this KRED enzyme (after only five rounds), this dynamics-based methodology identifies a distal mutation that was incorporated during experiment-based directed evolution. This work provides a novel foundation for computationally driven directed evolution efforts, opening the opportunity to simultaneously pursue and evaluate multiple evolutionary routes through a physics-based lens.

item.title: Computational Design and Evaluation of De Novo Protein Minibinders Targeting Specific Sites of STAT3
item.abstract: STAT3 is a transcription factor involved in the progression of many types of cancer, which makes it an attractive therapeutic target. Small-molecule STAT3 inhibitors have experienced a high failure rate in clinical trials, indicating alternative approaches may be warranted. To address these limitations, we used BindCraft, a modern AI-driven protein design tool, to create miniprotein binder candidates against several sites of STAT3. We selected seven target hotspots on the SH2, linker, DNA-binding and coiled-coil domains of STAT3. Of 139 designs that passed BindCraft's filters, 11 high-confidence binders emerged from five of the seven hotspots. These candidate binders were evaluated with AlphaFold3 (AF3). All eleven are predicted to dock with their intended domain; most within 4.5 [A] of one or more of their targeted hotspot residues. Several minibinders are predicted to dock simultaneously to STAT3 without overlap. Such pairs have the potential to constitute STAT3 sandwich assays. BLASTp searches found no matches with known protein sequences for six of the binders and only very low-significance matches for the other five. We disclose herein the sequences of our top binders targeting diverse regions of the STAT3 surface with the hope that experimental validation by the broader research community will yield promising leads for preclinical drug development against this important cellular regulator.

item.title: Engineering Methylobacterium as a C1 biomanufacturing platform: Metabolic architecture, regulatory networks, and synthetic biology strategies.
item.abstract: Methanol is emerging as a sustainable and energy-dense one carbon (C1) feedstock for next-generation biomanufacturing, owing to its superior energy density, abundance, water miscibility, and decoupling from food supply chains. Methylobacterium species are facultative methylotrophs that have evolved sophisticated metabolic and regulatory networks for efficient methanol utilization. This review highlights the transition of Methylobacterium from a model organism for dissecting methylotrophy to a programmable C1 chassis for synthetic biology. We provide a unique overview of its core metabolic architecture, focusing on the lanthanide-switchable pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ)-dependent methanol oxidation, the tetrahydromethanopterin (H₄MPT)-mediated formaldehyde buffering system, and the tight coupling of the serine cycle with the ethylmalonyl-CoA (EMC) pathway, which together govern carbon flux, redox balance, and energy efficiency. Building on this intrinsic framework, we survey how these traits are leveraged to produce high-value chemicals, such as folate derivatives, redox cofactors, organic acids, terpenoids, bioplastics, and single-cell protein. Furthermore, we discuss advanced engineering strategies for systematic chassis optimization including global transcriptional regulation, metabolic valve control, and photo-methylotrophic configurations, along with a comprehensive evaluation of Methylobacterium chassis advantages and disadvantages, concrete product-chassis matching rules, common engineering bottlenecks, and diversified low-cost feedstock options. Finally, we propose a product-chassis matching framework and outline future directions centered on regulatory control, flux coordination, and robustness enhancement to overcome current limitations in titer, yield, and scale-up, while also leveraging agricultural applications and low-cost feedstocks, thereby positioning Methylobacterium as a cornerstone of sustainable low-carbon biotechnology.

item.title: Design Space Exploration of Genetic Circuits Using the UNFOLD Framework.
item.abstract: In this chapter, we describe UNFOLD (UNified FramewOrk for reguLatory Dynamics), a comprehensive computational approach for exploring the design space of gene regulatory circuits and characterizing fundamental biological properties. UNFOLD enables systematic analysis of how three-node genetic circuits can exhibit properties such as robustness, plasticity, evolvability, and functional canalization. Through exhaustive simulation of over 190 million genetic circuits covering all possible three-node network structures, we identify the complete functional repertoire achievable by such circuits and establish quantitative relationships between circuit structure, parameters, and function. The framework introduces three key diversity metrics: structural diversity, parametric diversity, and functional diversity, which together provide a unified mathematical basis for understanding biological resilience. We demonstrate that only 20 distinct functions are achievable with three-node circuits, that every network exhibits multifunctionality, and that significant network degeneracy allows multiple structural implementations of the same function. We detail the computational pipeline for finding the functional repertoire, the methodology for calculating diversity metrics, and procedures for identifying circuits with specific biological properties. The UNFOLD framework implementation is available from https://github.com/RamanLab/UNFOLD-Framework .

item.title: Synthetic Gene Circuit Analysis and Optimization.
item.abstract: Synthetic biology aims to engineer synthetic circuits with predefined target functions. From a systems (model-based) perspective, two problems are of central importance: (i) given a model of a biomolecular circuit, determining whether it is capable of exhibiting a specific behavior or functionality; and (ii) starting from a predefined required functionality and a library of biological parts, identifying the biomolecular circuit that, when constructed as a combination of such parts, achieves the desired behavior. These two problems, which can be framed, respectively, as nonlinear analysis and automated design problems, are addressed here using efficient optimization methods. In this chapter, we specifically focus on deterministic frameworks, in which the effect of intrinsic molecular noise on the dynamics is not significant. We illustrate these methods through case studies focused on the analysis and design of biocircuits capable of bistability (bistable switches). Bistability is of particular interest in systems and synthetic biology because it endows cells with the capacity to make decisions.

item.title: Computational Design of Prokaryotic Translation Regulation Based on RNA-Binding Proteins.
item.abstract: Translation regulation enables precise control of protein expression levels. In prokaryotes, regulatory RNAs and RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) can modulate ribosome activity at the level of translation initiation. Here, we examine the computational design of RBP-based translation regulation systems. We first present a systematic exploration of protein databases and genomic datasets to identify candidate regulatory RBPs. We then describe the design of target RNA sequences required to achieve distinct regulatory behaviors. We show how model-based experimental characterization provides quantitative insight into regulatory performance and enables rational comparison among different designs. Finally, we present omics-based approaches to evaluate the orthogonality of the engineered systems within the host organism. Overall, our procedure outlines the main stages for engineering RBP-mediated translation control and provides a synthetic biology framework for programming bacterial cells.

item.title: Expression of Human CYP2D6 in Artificial Cells Based on Polymer-Lipid Hybrid Vesicles.
item.abstract: Artificial cells with the ability to express functional, biomedically relevant enzymes have long been a goal in the field of bottom-up synthetic biology. Here, we demonstrate the expression of human cytochrome P450 2D6 (CYP2D6) within the lumen of giant hybrid vesicle-based artificial cells using a cell-free protein expression system based on the protozoan Leishmania tarentolae. The vesicle membranes comprise 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine and amphiphilic block copolymers containing poly(cholesteryl methacrylate-co-butyl methacrylate) with either poly(galactose methacrylate) (pGalacMA) or poly(carboxyethyl acrylate) as the hydrophilic block. The amount and composition of the block copolymer incorporated into the giant hybrid vesicle membrane altered the artificial cells' ability to support functional protein expression, likely through changes in membrane properties. In particular, giant hybrid vesicles containing pGalacMA supported production of enzymatically active CYP2D6. Overall, the reported approach advances the development of artificial cells capable of producing functional, biomedically relevant enzymes. Further, the effort highlights complex interplay between polymer properties and performance of biological components in the functional complexity achievable in polymer-lipid hybrid vesicles.

item.title: Meta-Scoring Approach to Curate Synthetic RNA 3D Structures.
item.abstract: The structural diversity of RNA is central to molecular medicine, RNA-targeted drug discovery, and synthetic biology, where engineered RNA molecules are increasingly used in therapeutic, regulatory, and nanotechnology applications. While the rapid development of deep learning methods has heightened the demand for large, diverse structural datasets, high-quality RNA data remain scarce compared to protein datasets. Synthetic RNA structure datasets can help address this gap by enabling large-scale exploration of conformational space; however, their practical utility depends on careful curation and validation to ensure reliability. Here, we present a pipeline, RNA-SyntHub, for systematically constructing curated synthetic RNA datasets. The workflow integrates data from multiple structure-generation approaches with a meta-scoring function to identify low-quality models and select high-confidence candidates. As a proof of concept, we applied this method to a dataset of 447,402 synthetic RNA structures predicted by RFDiffusion, obtaining a curated subset of approximately 16,000 structures, further complemented with predictions from Boltz-1 and RNAComposer. This study provides both a methodological framework for generating and curating large collections of synthetic RNA 3D models under explicitly stated assumptions and a concrete dataset that supports methodological development, exploratory analyses, decoy-based applications, and selected deep learning workflows in RNA design, synthetic biology, and nanotechnology.

item.title: Deep mutational scanning of the GPCR rhodopsin reveals pleiotropic mutational effects and their roles in modulating receptor signaling.
item.abstract: Biophysical pleiotropy, the phenomenon in which a mutation affects multiple protein properties, underlies many genetic diseases and shapes protein evolution, yet remains poorly understood, limiting synthetic biology and therapeutic development. Although extensively studied in soluble proteins, little is known about how pleiotropic effects shaped the evolution of receptor protein functions. Here, we developed a cell-based assay designed to assess pleiotropic effects in G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), the largest receptor class in eukaryotes. Because our assay allows for multiple GPCR molecular phenotypes (basal activity, ligand-dependent signaling, and cellular receptor abundance) to be simultaneously assessed, we applied it to study rhodopsin, a visual GPCR that evolved for high phototransduction capabilities by maximizing light-driven responses while minimizing noise. To investigate this, we integrated our assay with deep mutational scanning to test the impacts of ~2,000 single-residue substitutions in rhodopsin across all three molecular phenotypes (~6,000 measurements). By analyzing these data in the context of rhodopsin's protein structures, we found complex pleiotropic effects that act asymmetrically to impose joint constraints, restricting mutational tolerance in rhodopsin's retinal binding pocket and G protein interaction interface. A dose-response analysis of rhodopsin signaling revealed that these pleiotropic constraints arise from the dual functions of its chromophore, which acts as an agonist upon light-driven isomerization but also an inverse agonist in darkness. Because these constraints reflect mechanistically driven limitations in the evolution of receptor signaling, these findings reveal a role for biophysical pleiotropy in shaping the signaling capabilities of receptor proteins.

item.title: Genome-Scale Metabolic Modeling of Escherichia coli and Its Chassis Design for Synthetic Biology Applications.
item.abstract: Genome-scale metabolic modeling is and will continue to play a central role in computational systems metabolic engineering and synthetic biology applications for the production of chemicals and antibiotics. To that end, a survey and workflows of methods used for the development of high-quality genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) and chassis design for synthetic biology are described here. The chapter consists of two parts (a) the methods of development of GEMs (Escherichia coli as a case study) and (b) E. coli chassis design for synthetic production of 1, 4-butanediol (BDO). Additionally, a case study of an engineered E. coli synthetically producing paracetamol from plastic waste is summarized. The methods described here can guide existing and future development of GEMs coupled with host chassis design for the synthetic production of novel materials, fuels, chemicals, and therapeutics.

item.title: Fine-Tuning a Protein Language Model for Epitope Library Generation and Sequence Filtering.
item.abstract: Linear peptide epitopes play a key role in vaccines, immunotherapies, and diagnostics, yet discovering them remains difficult because peptide sequence space grows exponentially and experimentally confirmed epitopes are relatively few. This chapter presents a computational framework for the generation of synthetic linear epitope libraries that reproduce key statistical and sequence-level properties of naturally occurring epitopes. A large language model pre-trained on protein sequences and subsequently fine-tuned on curated epitope datasets is employed to generate biologically plausible peptide candidates beyond those observed experimentally. To further enrich functional relevance of the generated sequences, they are filtered using transformer-based classification models trained on viral and bacterial epitope datasets. These models are applied as discriminative tools to distinguish likely epitopes from non-epitopes rather than to infer pathogen origin. The resulting libraries are designed to be compatible with high-throughput experimental screening platforms, such as droplet microfluidics, enabling efficient integration of generative artificial intelligence with experimental immunology workflows.

item.title: Roads not taken: The mismatch between safety and regulation of plant breeding innovation.
item.abstract: Meeting global food security goals while reducing agriculture's environmental impact requires continued crop improvement and innovation. Advances in transgenesis, cisgenesis, and genome editing now enable increasingly precise genetic modification with risks comparable to those of conventional breeding, yet regulatory frameworks remain focused on the method used rather than the product. We highlight recent examples, including immune receptor transfer, cisgenesis-based disease resistance stacking, photosynthesis engineering, and AI-guided protein design, that illustrate innovations constrained by current regulatory approaches. A decisive shift toward science-based, proportionate, and product-focused regulation is needed so that improved crops are evaluated on the basis of their properties, not how they were made.

item.title: Quantifying Turnover in Resource Economy of Synthetic Biology Applications via Stochastic Simulations.
item.abstract: We present a quantitative framework for analyzing resource turnover in synthetic biology applications using stochastic simulation of chemical reaction networks (CRNs). Building on a conservative extension of Gillespie's stochastic simulation algorithm, our method tracks causal dependencies between reaction events to generate flux graphs that represent resource flow dynamics. We illustrate how these graphs complement conventional trajectory analyses by enabling comparative assessment of cellular resource expenditure across different model parameter regimes. As a case study, we examine the E. coli two-component system responsible for inorganic phosphate uptake and demonstrate how synthetic promoter variants affect ATP-related resource economy. This framework supports predictive, model-based design for optimizing energy efficiency in living technologies.

item.title: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences
item.abstract: OpenAI will honor a shared robots.txt signal to help website operators communicate their AI training preferences to participating providers.

cards.score_reason: OpenAI训练数据政策影响AI合规
cards.title_cn: OpenAI 支持共享 robots.txt 信号，网站可统一表达 AI 训练偏好
cards.one_liner: OpenAI 将遵循共享 robots.txt 信号，让网站统一向参与方表达 AI 训练偏好。
key_findings: OpenAI 宣布采纳共享 robots.txt 信号，用于传达 AI 训练偏好。
该信号面向参与该机制的 AI 提供方，网站可一次声明偏好。
这是行业协作机制，非单方面技术限制。
cards.why_it_matters: 数据合规与训练语料来源是合成生物学 AI 模型的关键风险点，该机制影响未来公开数据获取与合规成本。

cards.one_liner: 富士胶片计划将磁带产能扩大5倍，以应对AI带来的数据归档需求增长。
key_findings: 低成本与离线安全性使磁带在归档场景中仍有不可替代的价值
AI发展带动冷数据归档需求，磁带作为存储介质需求回升
富士胶片大幅扩产，反映产业对磁带长期需求的信心
cards.why_it_matters: 合成生物学研究产生海量测序与实验数据，低成本离线归档方案对数据长期保存与合规管理有直接参考价值。

item.title: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals
item.abstract: While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents […]

cards.score_reason: AI智能体科研应用有趣
cards.title_cn: 夜间鸣响之物：Agentic AI 加入搜寻地外信号
cards.one_liner: NVIDIA 报道称，Agentic AI 已用于搜寻地外智能信号，并关注人类构建的 AI agent 监听 AI agent 信号。
key_findings: 搜寻地外智能（SETI）借助 AI 取得重大进展，AI 成为信号搜寻的新工具。
重点转向由人类构建的 AI agent，去监听可能来自 AI agent 的信号。
报道来自 NVIDIA Newsroom，属科技产业动态而非同行评议研究。
cards.why_it_matters: 对合成生物学读者而言，这提示 agentic AI 在自动化科学发现中的落地路径，可借鉴其自主搜索与筛选范式，但与本领域直接关联有限。

item.title: Fair use benefits everyone
item.abstract: OpenAI shares excerpts from court briefs by creators, academics, accessibility advocates, and legal experts, among others, on how fair use supports AI training and innovation.

cards.score_reason: 合理使用法律议题相关
cards.title_cn: OpenAI 援引创作者与学界意见，主张合理使用利于 AI 训练与创新
cards.one_liner: OpenAI 公开法院意见书节选，以创作者、学者与法律专家观点论证合理使用支撑 AI 训练。
key_findings: OpenAI 汇总创作者、学者、无障碍倡导者及法律专家的法庭意见书节选
核心主张是合理使用制度支撑 AI 训练与创新
内容来自 OpenAI News，属公司立场性披露
cards.why_it_matters: 合理使用是 AI 训练数据合规的关键变量，影响生物医药等领域的模型数据获取与知识产权边界，值得跟踪判例走向。

cards.score_reason: 企业案例营销内容

cards.one_liner: Credit Saison 试点 ChatGPT Enterprise 获 954% ROI，并推广至全公司。
